notes:
Task and constraints: Produce the nth string in the count-and-say sequence, with 1 <= n <= 30; each term describes consecutive equal digits in the preceding term.
Idea: Start with term = "1". For each of the next n-1 terms, scan term using i and j to find the maximal run of the same digit, append the run length and that digit to out, then join out into the next term.
Technique and why it applies: Run-length encoding converts each contiguous run into a count-digit pair, exactly matching how the next count-and-say term is defined.
Invariant: At the start of each outer scan, term is the complete sequence term for the previous step; as i advances, out encodes every character before i as its run count followed by the run's digit.
Edge cases: n=1 skips the outer loop and returns "1". For term "11", the scan emits "21" for the single two-character run. When adjacent digits differ, j stops immediately and each run is encoded separately.
Complexity: If T is the total number of characters scanned and emitted across all generated terms, time is O(T); auxiliary space is O(L) for the current and next terms, where L is the larger term length.
complexity_reason: Each iteration scans every character of the current term once, emits two pieces per run into out, and replaces term with the joined output.

notes:
Task and constraints: Return the nth count-and-say string for 1 <= n <= 30 by describing consecutive equal digits in the preceding term.
Idea: Initialize term to "1" and repeat n-1 times. The inner loop uses i and j to measure a run, appends j-i and term.charAt(i) to StringBuilder out, advances i to j, then converts out to the next term.
Technique and why it applies: Run-length encoding maps each maximal run of identical characters to its length and character, which is precisely the sequence's construction rule.
Invariant: Before each run is processed, positions before i have already been represented in out; j advances only across characters equal to term.charAt(i), so the appended count describes exactly that run.
Edge cases: For n=1, no conversion occurs and "1" is returned. A run such as "111" emits "31". StringBuilder avoids repeatedly rebuilding an immutable string for each count-digit append; charAt accesses remain within the run's bounds.
Complexity: If T is the total length of all terms scanned and generated, time is O(T); auxiliary space is O(L) for term and StringBuilder out, where L is the larger of the current and next term lengths.
complexity_reason: Each step visits every character in term once, appends one count and digit per run to StringBuilder, and materializes the next term.
